figures.title: SD Specifications Documentation Structure
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the hierarchical structure of SD Specifications documentation, with Application Specifications (Audio, Video, Other) at the top layer, File System in the middle, and Physical Layer, Security, Advanced Security SD Extension, and SDIO specifications at the foundation level.

figures.title: "no response" and "no data" Operations
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates two types of SD bus operations: a "no response" operation where the host sends a command with no card response, and a "no data" operation where the host sends a command and receives a response but no data is transferred on the DAT line.

figures.title: (Multiple) Block Read Operation
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates the SD bus protocol for single and multiple block read operations, showing the CMD line carrying host commands and card responses while the DAT line transfers multiple data blocks with CRC, terminated by a stop command from the host.

figures.title: (Multiple) Block Write Operation
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates the SD card multiple block write operation showing the CMD line carrying command/response pairs while the DAT line transfers data blocks followed by CRC and busy signals, with a stop command terminating the transfer.

figures.title: Command Token Format
figures.abstract: Figure 3-4 shows the 48-bit command token format for SD card communication, consisting of a start bit (0), transmitter bit (1 for host), command content with address/parameter information, 7-bit CRC checksum, and end bit (1).

figures.title: Response Token Format
figures.abstract: This figure shows the two response token formats used in SD card communication: a 48-bit format (R1, R3, R6) containing start bit, transmitter bit, content, and end bit, and a 136-bit format (R2) that additionally includes CID or CSD content with a separate CRC field.

figures.title: Data Packet Format - Usual Data
figures.abstract: This figure illustrates the SD card data packet format for both standard bus (1-bit mode using only DAT0) and wide bus (4-bit mode using DAT0-DAT3), showing how 8-bit data bytes are serialized with start bit, data bytes (LSB first), CRC, and end bit, with wide bus mode distributing bits across four data lines (b7/b3 on DAT3, b6/b2 on DAT2, b5/b1 on DAT1, b4/b0 on DAT0).

figures.title: Data Packet Format - Wide Width Data
figures.abstract: This figure illustrates the SD card data packet format for wide width data transfers, showing both the standard bus format using only DAT0 and the wide bus format using all four data lines (DAT0-DAT3) with interleaved bit distribution, start/end bits, and CRC fields.

figures.title: UHS-I Card Type Modes of Operation versus Frequency Range
figures.abstract: This figure shows the supported operation modes for UHS50 and UHS104 SD card types across different frequency ranges (25MHz to 208MHz), indicating which modes use 3.3V signaling (DS, HS) versus 1.8V signaling (SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, SDR104, DDR50).

figures.title: UHS-I Card Type Modes of Operation versus Throughput
figures.abstract: This figure shows the supported speed modes and corresponding throughput capabilities for UHS50 and UHS104 SD cards, illustrating that UHS50 cards support modes up to 50MB/s while UHS104 cards additionally support SDR104 mode reaching 104MB/s throughput.

figures.title: Command Sequence to Use UHS-I
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the command sequence required to initialize and configure an SD card for UHS-I mode operation, starting from power-on through voltage switching, card identification, and bus speed mode selection.

figures.title: SD Memory Card State Diagram (card identification mode)
figures.abstract: This state diagram illustrates the SD Memory Card initialization sequence in card identification mode, showing transitions from power-on through Idle, Ready, Identification, and Stand-by states via various commands (CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3) with paths to Inactive state for incompatible cards.

figures.title: Card Initialization and Identification Flow (SD mode)
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the SD card initialization and identification sequence in SD mode, showing the command flow (CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD11, CMD2, CMD3) to detect card type, version, and capacity while handling various error conditions for unusable cards.

figures.title: Argument of ACMD41
figures.abstract: This figure shows the bit field layout of the ACMD41 command argument for SD card initialization, including fields for host capacity support, power control, voltage switching request, and OCR register values.

figures.title: Response of ACMD41
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 48-bit response format (R3) of ACMD41 command, detailing bit fields including Busy status, Card Capacity Status (CCS), S18A voltage switching acceptance flag, OCR register, and CRC7 checksum.

figures.title: ACMD41 Timing Followed by Voltage Switch Sequence
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the ACMD41 command sequence for SD card initialization, depicting repeated ACMD41 commands until the card is ready, followed by CMD11 to initiate voltage switch for UHS-I mode.

figures.title: UHS-I Host Initialization Flow Chart
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the UHS-I host initialization sequence for SD cards, showing the command flow from CMD0 through voltage switching, card capability detection, and tuning procedures to establish UHS-I mode operation.

figures.title: Voltage Switch Command
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the Voltage Switch Command (CMD11) format and protocol, depicting the command structure with index 001011, followed by the R1 response on the CMD line, while DAT[3:0] remains inactive.

figures.title: Send Tuning Block Command
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the CMD19 Send Tuning Block Command sequence where the host sends CMD19 on the CMD line and receives an R1 response followed by a 128-bit tuning block pattern data block on DAT[3:0] within 146 clock cycles.

figures.title: SD Memory Card State Diagram (data transfer mode)
figures.abstract: This state diagram illustrates the SD Memory Card data transfer mode states and transitions, showing how commands (CMD0-CMD56, ACMD) move the card between Stand-by, Transfer, Sending-data, Receive-data, Programming, and Disconnect states.

figures.title: Use of Switch Command
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates the CMD6 switch command operation in two modes: Mode 0 (Check function) for querying supported functions, and Mode 1 (Switch function) for changing card functionality, showing the CMD and DAT line sequences including card internal execution, status data response, and the function change timing constraint of within 8 clocks.

figures.title: Busy Status of 'Command System'
figures.abstract: Figure 4-11 shows the busy status bit layout for Function Group 2 (Command System) spanning bits 303-288, where each bit indicates ready (0) or busy (1) status for functions including VS, ASSD, and eC.

figures.title: CRC7 Generator/Checker
figures.abstract: This figure shows a 7-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) circuit implementing the CRC7 generator/checker with polynomial G(x) = x⁷ + x³ + 1, featuring seven D flip-flops and two XOR gates at the x⁰ and x³ tap positions for feedback.

figures.title: CRC16 Generator/Checker
figures.abstract: A 16-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) implementation of the CRC16 generator/checker using the CCITT polynomial G(x) = x¹⁶ + x¹² + x⁵ + 1, with XOR feedback taps at bit positions 5 and 12, used for payload protection in SD card block transfer mode.

figures.title: Overview of Speed Class Specification
figures.abstract: This figure shows a matrix of SD card speed class specifications, indicating that Class 2, 4, and 6 are available in Default Speed Mode for Standard Capacity, SDHC, and SDXC cards, while Class 10 requires High Speed Mode and is only available for SDHC and SDXC cards, with the 'r' parameter indicating fragmented vs sequential write modes.

figures.title: Definition of Allocation Unit (AU)
figures.abstract: This figure illustrates how the User Area of an SD card is divided into Allocation Units (AUs), where each AU contains multiple Recording Units (RUs), with the number of RUs per AU calculated as m = S_AU/S_RU.

figures.title: Three Performance Curves
figures.abstract: This figure shows three SD card performance curves (Class 0/2, 4, and 6) plotting write performance (MB/sec) against the ratio of used Recording Units (RU), where all curves decrease as the card fills up and intersect at point (1,0) when fully utilized.

figures.title: Example Erase Characteristics (Case 1 TOFFSET=0)
figures.abstract: This figure shows a linear graph depicting the relationship between the number of Allocation Units (AUs) erased and the erase timeout in seconds, where Line A represents the timeout characteristic starting from the origin (T_OFFSET=0) with T_ERASE defining the timeout value at a given N_ERASE count.

figures.title: Example Erase Characteristics (Case 2 TOFFSET=2)
figures.abstract: This graph shows the linear relationship between erase timeout (in seconds) and the number of Allocation Units (AUs) erased, where Line B starts at T_OFFSET=2 seconds and increases proportionally up to T_ERASE as more AUs are erased.

figures.title: Set Block Count Command
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates the Set Block Count Command (CMD23) structure showing the command format with 32-bit block count field, followed by the command sequence where CMD23 with R1 response precedes a CMD18/25 read/write operation.

figures.title: ERASE_BLK_EN = 0 Example
figures.abstract: This figure illustrates how erase operations work when ERASE_BLK_EN=0, showing that the erase area extends from the beginning of the sector containing the start address to the end of the sector containing the end address, with erase units being full SECTOR_SIZE blocks.

figures.title: ERASE_BLK_EN = 1 Example
figures.abstract: This figure illustrates the erase operation when ERASE_BLK_EN=1, showing that the host can erase data in 512-byte units where only the exact range from start address (5) to end address (40) is erased, matching the host-specified address range precisely.

figures.title: Change of Figure for Power Up
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates the SD card power-up sequence showing voltage levels from power-on cycle (below 0.5V for >1ms), through power ramp up, to stable operating supply range (2.7V-3.6V), followed by initialization sequence before CMD0 can be issued.

figures.title: SD Memory Card State Diagram (SPI mode)
figures.abstract: This state diagram illustrates the SD Memory Card initialization sequence in SPI mode, showing the transition from power-on through idle state to data-transfer mode using commands CMD0, CMD8, CMD58, and ACMD41, with branches for handling legacy cards and error conditions.

figures.title: SPI Mode Initialization Flow
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the SPI mode initialization sequence for SD Memory Cards, showing the command flow (CMD0, CMD8, CMD58, ACMD41) to identify card type (Ver1.X Standard Capacity, Ver2.00 Standard Capacity, or High/Extended Capacity) and detect unusable cards based on voltage compatibility and response patterns.

figures.title: Single Block Read Operation
figures.abstract: Figure 7-3 illustrates the SPI mode single block read operation timing, showing the host sending a command on DataIn, followed by the card's response, data block, and CRC on DataOut, before the next command can be issued.

figures.title: Read Operation - Data Error
figures.abstract: Figure 7-4 shows the SPI timing diagram for a read operation that encounters a data retrieval error, where the card sends a data error token instead of actual data in response to a host command.

figures.title: Multiple Block Read Operation
figures.abstract: Figure 7-5 illustrates the SPI mode multiple block read operation timing, showing the host sending a command on DataIn, followed by the card responding with multiple data blocks each suffixed with CRC on DataOut, until a stop transmission command is issued.

figures.title: Single Block Write Operation
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates a single block write operation in SPI mode, showing the host sending a command followed by a data block with start token, and the card responding with a response token, data_response, and busy signal before the next command can be issued.

figures.title: Multiple Block Write Operation
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates the SPI bus transaction sequence for a multiple block write operation, showing the DataIn line carrying commands and data blocks from host to card, and the DataOut line carrying responses and busy signals from card to host, terminated by a Stop Tran Token.

figures.title: 'No data' Operations
figures.abstract: Figure 7-8 illustrates the timing of 'no data' bus operations in SPI mode, showing the sequence of command and response exchanges on DataIn and DataOut lines, with the card entering a busy state after the second response without any data transfer phase.

figures.title: R1 Response Format
figures.abstract: The R1 response format is a single-byte response token used in SD card SPI mode, with bit 7 always zero and bits 6-0 representing various error and status flags including parameter error, address error, erase sequence error, CRC error, illegal command, erase reset, and idle state indicators.

figures.title: R2 Response Format
figures.abstract: This figure shows the R2 response format, a 2-byte response token for the SEND_STATUS command, with the first byte identical to R1 and the second byte containing status flags for card lock, write protection, ECC, and various error conditions.

figures.title: R3 Response Format
figures.abstract: This figure shows the R3 response format, a 40-bit response token sent by an SD card in reply to a READ_OCR command, consisting of a start bit, R1 response byte, and 32-bit OCR register contents.

figures.title: R7 Response Format
figures.abstract: The R7 response format is a 40-bit (5-byte) response token sent by the SD card in reply to SEND_IF_COND (CMD8), containing an R1 status byte, command version, reserved bits, voltage accepted indicator, and an echo-back check pattern.

figures.title: Data Error Token
figures.abstract: Figure 7-13 shows the 8-bit Data Error Token format used in SPI mode when a read operation fails, with the upper 4 bits fixed at zero and the lower 4 bits containing error flags for out of range, Card ECC Failed, CC Error, and general Error conditions.
